purpose: Codex-only successor of generator-multimodel-v1. In v1 the Codex rows were harness-limited: arm A was not the official MCP generator for most Codex models (gpt-5.5 pilot: 6 of 12 A cells had a child agent report the generator tools were not exposed, the other 6 unknown; gpt-6-sol delivered 3 of 12 A cells; gpt-6-astra 0 of 12 in every arm). This protocol uses 72 cells per model (4 repetitions) and the owner-approved compatibility and analysis changes, then separates cells where the official tools demonstrably ran from the rest.
v1_codex_rows_status: harness-limited descriptive. The v1 Codex results are neither replaced, corrected nor re-read as quality differences by this protocol.

load.rule: Inherited wait: a cell waits (60 s steps, at most 1800 s) while the 1-minute load average is above 40, then starts regardless. The load average is recorded at the start of every cell. A cell whose load_at_start is above 40 is FLAGGED, never dropped. Flagged cells stay in the primary view; the load_clean view recomputes the labels without them as a sensitivity.

output_root: ~/.cache/e2e-skills-bench/multimodel-v2-codex (override: MULTIMODEL_V2_CODEX_DIR); per model: <root>/<model>/{final.json,scores.json,results.json,final-artifacts/,final-transcripts/,codex-sessions/}; entry decisions in <root>/_entry/<model>.json; the harness live check in <root>/_entry/harness-check.json; progress in <root>/STATUS.md

unchanged: seed and two-phase scheduling algorithm (phase 1 A and C shuffled, phase 2 B shuffled)
container image, network, effort (medium), timeout (1500 s)
scoring engine, scanner, skill snapshots, reviewer prompt (arm B)
the frozen v1 runner, pilot scorer and engine, imported unchanged

adapter_flags.file: scripts/evals/generator_codex_official_adapter_compat.py (separate file; the frozen generator_codex_official_adapter.py is untouched and stays bound by the v1 freeze)
adapter_flags.removed_all_arms: --ephemeral. Diagnosis: with multi_agent_version v2 a spawned agent forks the parent rollout, and an ephemeral parent has none ('no rollout found').
adapter_flags.added_arm_a_only: Session-wide playwright-test MCP command, args, PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and HOME; enabled_tools restricted to the 19 generator/browser tools in the pinned official generator definition; read-only session sandbox so the generating generic child inherits the official role restriction as far as Codex configuration allows. Native tools remain available for delegation and reads. Configuration acceptance, child inheritance, denied direct writes and hidden planner/healer tools require a live check. Approved 2026-10-15.
adapter_flags.identical_otherwise: Arms B and C retain the frozen argv apart from removal of --ephemeral and per-cell sessions persistence. Arm A additionally sets the generator-only MCP allowlist and read-only sandbox; offline argv tests verify the differences.
adapter_flags.added_all_arms_sessions: A per-call host directory is bind-mounted at /sessions-out and symlinked as $CODEX_HOME/sessions (one extra `ln -s` line in the container script, a symlink rather than a nested mount so that no root-owned directory is created inside the /codex-home tmpfs). After the container is removed its rollouts are copied, sanitised like the transcript, to <model dir>/codex-sessions/<transcript stem>/. Same for every arm. The argv helper without a sessions argument is unchanged, which the offline test diffs against the frozen adapter.

arm_a_prompt_line.v1: Delegate to a native agent that is the `playwright_test_generator` custom agent ('spawn it as a native agent').
arm_a_prompt_line.v2: Spawn a native agent (generic: the spawn tool has no agent-type selector), give it the generator definition from .codex/agents/playwright_test_generator.toml as instructions, and state that the generator's MCP server (playwright-test, same command as its definition) is already configured for the whole session. Unchanged: do not write or edit specs yourself, no planner or healer, one verification run allowed, the per-row approval for `npx playwright run-test-mcp-server`, and the instruction to stop with partial_or_blocked if no agent can be spawned or cannot set up its browser.
arm_a_prompt_line.why: In v2-catalog models the v1 wording asked for something the spawn tool cannot do (astra, 12 of 12 A cells: 'cannot select the custom playwright_test_generator agent or load its MCP tools').

arm_c_scratch_sentence.text: Writing the skill's temporary exploration/guard config and scratch files outside the project directory (for example under /tmp) is also approved; it does not count as editing files outside tests/ in the project.
arm_c_scratch_sentence.why: The v1 arm C frame forbids writes outside tests/ while the skill asks for a guard config outside the worktree; the sentence removes that contradiction and is appended to the v1 arm C line only.

changes_vs_v1.diagnosis_status: The diagnosis agent's report was only partly verified. Verified for this protocol: the local Codex model cache lists multi_agent_version v2 for gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra and v1 for gpt-5.6-luna; the stored v1 transcripts show the refusals (gpt-6-astra 12 of 12 A cells: cannot select the custom agent or load its MCP tools; gpt-6-sol 9 of 12 A cells blocked, 8 with 'tools unavailable' and 1 failing to spawn); the compat-diag runs produced specs on astra and sol (one or two runs each). Not re-observed: the 'no rollout found' failure of --ephemeral and the claim that the compat adapter is what makes the difference (single runs, no control). Second round (harness fixes H1 to H8): the port conflict, the 400-character command cut, the invisibility of child agents in the parent stream and the minimal treatment on sonnet were re-derived from stored files by an independent audit; the fixes are offline-tested against synthetic data and stored cells, and the live checks in README section 'Live check after freeze' are still open.

generation_config.what: In the generation phase every arm's staged project carries playwright.config.mjs with `reuseExistingServer: true` instead of the case's frozen `reuseExistingServer: false`. Nothing else in the config differs.
generation_config.why: In the v1 Claude campaign the parent's single verification run of `playwright test` failed with 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health is already used' in 12 of 12 sonnet arm-A cells before any test started: the official generator's MCP session keeps the app server alive on that port. Arms B and C did not hit it. On Codex, gpt-6-sol arm A reports the same symptom.
generation_config.scope: Generation only, all three arms identically (arm B's reviewer call is a generation-phase call). The swap is an engine.stage wrapper active only inside one_call; scoring stages through the unmodified engine.stage with the frozen configs (reuseExistingServer false, clean environment, so that a leftover server cannot serve the original app instead of a mutant). The deliverable is tests/ only, so the generation config cannot reach scoring through files.
generation_config.proof: Offline tests stage a project per arm through the real v1 one_call and assert: generation config true for A, B and C and identical across them (port-normalised digest), the same file staged by the scoring path is false, engine.stage is restored after every call (also on an exception), and `scoring_guard` refuses to score while the wrapper is active or if a case config is not the frozen shape. Each cell records the digests; analyze raises if one case has two generation digests.
generation_config.not_done: Not observed live: that reuseExistingServer true removes the port conflict for the Codex arm A. The live check does not exercise it. It is the first thing to read in the first preflight cells (a parent `playwright test` result without the 'is already used' error).

roster_note: The roster is the Codex models of v1 whose catalog entry says multi_agent_version v2, because the compat changes target that spawn behaviour. At most 6 of the at most 8 Codex models; the entry rule decides which of them are scored.

excluded_models.reason: Catalog multi_agent_version v1: the spawn tool does have a role selector, so the v2 arm A line ('the spawn tool has no agent-type selector') would be false for it, and it engaged in the v1 preflight under the frozen harness. Its v1 rows stand as they are; a v2 rerun would need a different arm A treatment. It stays excluded under the owner-approved six-model roster (2026-10-15).

Unavailable on this account: HTTP 400, "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account", owner-verified 2026-10-14 23:50 KST. Finished pilot rows remain historical reference only, never in N; no planned call or dependency uses this model.
Hidden approval-reviewer model, as in v1.

entry_rule.proxy: The arm A fidelity class of a preflight call is 'official-tool' WITH HARD EVIDENCE: a completed generator_* or browser_* call on playwright-test (not test_* or planner_*) observed in the parent stream or in any rollout of the call (child agents included), or, when the rollout record is not complete, files under .playwright-mcp/ among the out-of-scope writes. An affirming message alone classifies a scored cell as official-tool (only without a complete rollout record) but never admits a model (the decision is final). A call with missing or incomplete primary evidence and no hard admission evidence is not an attempt (the model stays undecided), even when narration affirms success. The spec headers are not the proxy.
entry_rule.procedure: For every roster model, before any scored cell: up to 2 arm A calls on v2-01 (a task outside the preregistered set), plan and seed as in the scored cells, the compat harness. Only real attempts count; an aborted call (infrastructure outcome, see aborted_cell_rule) is never an attempt. The model is ADMITTED at the first attempt with an admitting classification; it is EXCLUDED only after 2 real attempts none of which admits, with the recorded reason and the classes of both attempts. Within one preflight invocation the first aborted call is rerun once (max_aborted_reruns); a second aborted call, or any usage/rate limit (fatal infrastructure), stops the invocation at once. Attempts and aborted calls accumulate in <root>/_entry/<model>.pending.json across invocations.
entry_rule.timing: All roster preflights are recorded before drive starts; drive refuses to run unless every roster model has a decision bound to the freeze. An admitted or excluded decision is final and is never repeated.
entry_rule.data_status: Preflight calls are never data: they are not scored, not analysed and not counted in any cell or N. Nothing is tuned on them.
entry_rule.undecided: A model whose preflight was interrupted by infrastructure before it has an admitting attempt or 2 real attempts is UNDECIDED: no decision file is written, the command exits 4, and the owner reruns it when the infrastructure is healthy. Infrastructure outages therefore never exclude a model. drive refuses to start while any roster model is undecided.
entry_rule.go_no_go: After the preflights, drive proceeds only if at least 4 models (decision.cross_model.min_models) over both lineages are admitted. Otherwise no cross-model verdict is possible and drive refuses unless the owner passes --descriptive-only, which runs the admitted models for per-model descriptive results only.
entry_rule.live_check_first: preflight runs the harness live check (harness_fixes.H3_child_agents.live_check) before its first entry call and exits 5 without any entry call if it is not a pass; a pass is kept in _entry/harness-check.json bound to the freeze and is not repeated. Exit codes: 0 decided, 4 undecided (infrastructure), 5 harness check not passed.

fidelity.scope: Arm A cells of every model; arm B cells inherit the class of their source arm A cell; arm C is not classified.

classes.official-tool: Positive evidence that the generator's MCP tools ran in that cell, delivered or not. PRIMARY (deterministic, observed): a completed call to a generator tool (generator_* or browser_*, the tool set of the generator agent definition) on server playwright-test in the parent JSON stream or in ANY rollout of the cell, child agents included (strength 'hard'). Completed test_* and planner_* calls on the same server are information only (other_playwright_test_calls), not evidence. The rollouts are the complete record only when there are no observation_gaps: the root rollout is identified, every unique spawned thread ID in the parent stream and all descendant rollouts has a persisted rollout with the expected parent relationship, and the persistence census has no skipped or errored entries. With a complete record, no generator call means none was made, the secondary evidence cannot make the cell positive, and a disagreement is recorded as signal_conflict. With rollouts but gaps and no hard positive signal the cell is observation_incomplete: the entry rule does not count it as an attempt (the model stays undecided). SECONDARY, used when the record is not complete (no rollouts, as in stored v1 cells, or observation gaps): (b) files under .playwright-mcp/ among the out-of-scope writes (strength 'hard'), then (c) an agent message (parent or child state) with a sentence that affirms the tools worked, carrying no negation (not, n't, never, no, unable, fail*, without, missing, lack*, if, whether) and no plan or intent wording (will, would, should, must, ask*, instruct*, 'to use/call/write'), in a message that matches no denial pattern (strength 'message'). The class means the generator's MCP tools demonstrably ran; it does NOT mean generator_write_test authored the spec (see role_differences).
classes.manual-follow: Delivered, no positive evidence, and at least one message denies the tools (not exposed / unavailable / cannot select or load / failed to spawn): the spec was written by following the definition by hand.
classes.unverified: Delivered, neither positive evidence nor a denial. Without rollouts, absence of a denial is not evidence of use; with rollouts present it means an observed absence of any playwright-test call (equivalent to manual-follow without a denial).
classes.blocked: No spec delivered and no positive evidence.
classes.aborted: Infrastructure outcome (see aborted_cell_rule); not a model outcome.

fidelity.headers_are_not_evidence: The first-party generator_write_test writes the model's code argument verbatim (playwright 1.62.0 lib/mcp/test/generatorTools.js); the '// spec:' and '// seed:' header comments come from the example inside the agent definition, so a model following the definition by hand writes them too. In the gpt-5.5 pilot, 5 of the 6 cells whose child said the tools were not exposed carry both headers. The v1 'official_signature' column therefore overstates fidelity and is kept in the records only as a labelled non-discriminating proxy. The child-rollout evidence replaces the headers and the messages as the primary signal.
fidelity.patterns: The denial and affirmation regular expressions (DENY, AFFIRM, NEG, INTENT) live in the runner and are bound by sha256 in the freeze. The first version was written after reading the gpt-5.5 pilot, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-astra and compat-diag transcripts and tested against exactly those stored cells; no transcript of any other model was seen. A review then found that the first AFFIRM accepted negations ('was not working', "isn't available", 'never called') and plan narration ('ask it to write via generator_write_test'); the revised patterns evaluate sentence by sentence with the NEG and INTENT guards, drop 'via/through <tool>' as evidence, and the test suite carries those sentences as negative controls. The patterns remain tuned on a small stored sample and are not validated on unseen transcripts.
fidelity.known_false_negatives: With rollouts: none known beyond a parser that does not recognise the container's rollout schema (the live check guards this). Without rollouts: a cell where the parent deletes the .playwright-mcp/ files before collection and never affirms the tools classifies as 'unverified' although the generator may have run (observed once in a compat-diag run).

views.primary: Arm A cells of class official-tool; arm B cells whose source A cell is official-tool; all arm C cells; aborted cells removed from every arm. The preregistered decision view.
views.itt: Intention-to-treat sensitivity: all 72 cells as run, aborted cells scored 0 as in v1.
views.upper: Sensitivity: like primary but arm A (and the source of arm B) may be official-tool or unverified.
views.load_clean: Sensitivity: primary without cells whose load_at_start is above 40.
views.as_treated: Sensitivity next to every primary label: arm A cells of class official-tool; arm B cells whose source A cell is official-tool and whose reviewer call read the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md and ran the scanner; arm C cells with treated_core (see fidelity.treatment). Aborted cells removed.

fidelity.role_differences: The pinned official generator definition restricts playwright-test to 19 generator/browser tools and sets sandbox_mode read-only. Compat arm A carries that allowlist session-wide and requests the read-only sandbox for both the parent and its generic generating child because the v2 spawn interface cannot select the custom role. The child follows the generator definition and writes through generator_write_test; planner/healer MCP tools are excluded. Configuration acceptance, generic-child inheritance and direct-write denial are unverified offline. generator_write_test writes code verbatim, so authorship is not recovered from headers; official-tool still means observed generator MCP use, never proof of authorship.
fidelity.known_false_positives: A message that affirms the tools in wording the guards do not recognise as negated or intended can still classify a cell as official-tool on message evidence alone (the entry rule is stricter: hard evidence only).

treatment.purpose: Treatment fidelity differs strongly by model (v1: gpt-5.5 arm C all key steps 10/12, gpt-6-sol 5/12, sonnet 0/12), so every per-model contrast is read with a fidelity table and an as-treated sensitivity, both defined here in advance.
arm_c_key_steps: reference_read (at least one other .md of the generator skill directory)
exploration (playwright cli, playwright-cli, agent-browser or run-raw-aria-snapshot in a command)
independent_review (the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md read AND an agent spawned in the stream)
treatment.arm_c_treated_core: skill_md_read AND reference_read AND scanner. The as-treated definition for arm C; fixed before any successor data is scored.
treatment.arm_b_treated: the e2e-reviewer SKILL.md read AND the scanner run in the reviewer call, on a source cell of class official-tool.
treatment.reporting: fidelity_table in results.json and the 'Treatment fidelity' summary section: counts of each step per model, treated cells per arm, and the primary-signal counts for arm A. A contrast whose as_treated label differs from the primary label is reported as depending on treatment fidelity; the primary label stays the pre-registered one.
treatment.known_limits: Step detection is by command text and tool-call path, not by outcome; a step 'done' can be perfunctory. as_treated selects arm C cells on behaviour after randomisation, like the primary view for arm A (per-protocol).

fidelity.rollout_completeness: A complete record identifies the root, reconciles every unique spawned thread ID in the parent and descendants against persisted parent relationships; unknown spawn identities and duplicate thread rollouts are gaps, has a clean persistence census and has no malformed rollout lines, unlinked children or extra roots. Incomplete records cannot supply a complete cost denominator; secondary fidelity evidence applies.

decision.no_p_values: No p-value, confidence interval, significance claim or PASS/FAIL release verdict in per-model labels or the cross-model rule. The separate pre-registered pooled analysis is approved 2026-10-15; it reports exact sign-flip p-values and two-way cluster-bootstrap intervals as development evidence and never replaces per-model labels.
decision.per_model_label: Restated from v1, applied to the cells of a view. A contrast X vs Y is EVALUABLE only if both arms have at least 6 delivered spec files among their cells in the view and the arms share at least 5 tasks (a task where either arm has no cell in the view cannot agree). If evaluable: 'suggestive: X better' if X's per-task refactor survival (mean over the view's repetitions of that task) is higher in at least 5 of the 6 tasks AND X's clean-3/3 rate, effective fault kill, scanner P0 and scanner P1/P2 are each not worse than Y's (scanner totals compared per cell, which equals v1's totals when both arms have the same number of cells; guards computed on the shared tasks); symmetric for Y; otherwise 'nothing'. Ties and 3-3 splits are 'nothing'. Otherwise 'not evaluable'. Same constants as v1 (6 delivered, 5 of 6 tasks).

cross_model.scope: Codex family only (the models of this protocol); decided on the primary view only; the other views are reported as sensitivities.
cross_model.rule: Per contrast, N = complete models (72 scored cells, at most 3 aborted cells) for which the contrast is evaluable in the primary view. N < 4: 'not evaluable'. Fewer than 2 lineages (gpt-6, gpt-5.6) among those N: 'not evaluable (single lineage)'. Otherwise 'consistent: X better in k of N models' only if at least max(2, ceil(N/3)) models carry 'suggestive: X better', none carries the opposite label, and the agreeing models span both lineages; otherwise 'not consistent' with the exact counts. No intermediate wording. 'consistent' is a descriptive count of agreeing models, not a replication or significance claim; for every feasible N (4 to 6) the threshold is simply 2 agreeing models.
cross_model.justification: Offline Monte Carlo, seed 20261016, 1500 replicates per cell, 6 tasks, 4 repetitions; evaluability retains >=6 official A cells on >=5 tasks (the simulation now uses the actual fixed min_delivered=6 rather than 3*repetitions). For a pilot-sized effect (logit +2.4, A 0.5 to C 0.917), the per-model positive-label rate is about 59% at perfect fidelity. Chosen-rule power at N=4/5/6 is 0.6727/0.7447/0.7933 at fidelity 1.0, 0.5373/0.6093/0.6720 at 0.75, 0.2073/0.2833/0.3260 at 0.5, and 0.0000/0.0033/0.0073 at 0.25. The v1 ceil(2N/3) threshold has power 0.5247 at N=6, fidelity 1.0. Worst-case false cross-model agreement in either direction across all null scenarios and fidelities, N=4..8, is 0.0447 with the lineage requirement (N6, shared-task null, fidelity 0.75), ABOVE the earlier 1% target; without the lineage requirement it is 0.0753. No decision threshold was changed: whether to recalibrate the agreement minimum or abandon the old target is an owner decision before freeze. At a floor of 3, maximum false agreement is 0.0127 and pilot-sized power 0.4827 at perfect fidelity. N is the number of admitted complete evaluable models, at most 6 in the roster; N8 and N3 are sensitivity scenarios only. The simulation ignores the guards and post-randomization selection of official A cells; results are not calibrated inferential guarantees. Low fidelity in stored v1 Codex cells (0 to 3 of 12) motivates entry/go-no-go checks before the 72-cell campaigns.
cross_model.verdict_wording: Earlier drafts called the positive verdict 'replicated'. It is renamed because for N = 4..6 it is a weak bar (two agreeing models, none opposite, both lineages) that a systematic harness artifact on the six fixtures would also clear.
cross_model.owner_option_min_agreeing_3: Raising min_agreeing to 3 would need the power table recomputed (it lowers power) and is not part of this protocol.
cross_model.owner_decision_after_recalculation: At 4 repetitions the unchanged chosen rule exceeds the earlier 1% simulated false-agreement target (4.47%). Owner must decide before freeze whether to retain this descriptive rule/target disclosure or recalibrate a threshold with a new simulation; this build preserves the approved scope and existing rule.

decision.incomplete_models: A model with fewer than 72 scored cells or more than 3 aborted cells is incomplete: shown descriptively, excluded from the labels and from N.
decision.reference_row: gpt-5.5 from the pilots is printed as a reference row only, never part of N.
decision.views_discordance: The primary view is the verdict. summary prints, per contrast, whether itt, upper and load_clean give a different cross-model verdict; a discordant sensitivity view is reported next to the primary one as 'depends on fidelity or load handling' and never overrides it. In load_clean an arm B cell is removed together with a load-flagged source arm A cell.
decision.conditioning: The primary view conditions arm A (and B) cells on a post-randomization variable (evidence that the tools ran, which may correlate with the outcome) while arm C is unconditioned: it is a per-protocol comparison, not a randomized one. itt and upper bracket it.

aborted_cell_rule: A cell is ABORTED when its call ends in an infrastructure outcome: infrastructure_error after the inherited single in-call retry, a usage/rate limit, a container or Docker failure, the disk floor, or an arm A setup UNAVAILABLE (init-agents failure or digest mismatch). The v2 runner sets infrastructure_error on a setup-UNAVAILABLE row (it is not set by the inherited v1 code), so the inherited rules apply to it: it is retried by later resumes at most twice and counts toward the three-in-a-row stop. A wall-clock timeout is NOT aborted (it is a model outcome: the cell is scored as run), and arm B with an empty source A deliverable is NOT aborted. Aborted cells are retried by later resumes at most twice (inherited), then stay recorded; they score 0 in the itt view and are removed from every arm in the primary, upper and load_clean views. Three consecutive infrastructure-error cells stop the campaign (inherited; a usage/rate limit stops it at once). More than 3 aborted cells make the model incomplete.

availability_signals: fidelity class and evidence counts (completed parent MCP events by tool, .playwright-mcp/ file count, affirming and denying message counts, transcript found, delivered, spec headers present)
setup status and agent-file digests (arm A)
spawn and wait census from the adapter (agent_spawns, collab tool calls, item types)
aborted flag and the error text of every attempt
timing: cell_started_utc and cell_finished_utc (the former is taken before any load wait)
evidence: rollouts: count of persisted rollouts, root found, linked/unlinked children, completed MCP calls by tool, child_usage, malformed lines (per cell, arm A fidelity also stores the same summary)

compliance_raw: untruncated counts from the raw transcript (skill/reference reads, preflight, scanner mention and exec runs, exploration, playwright test runs, agent spawns in stream, longest command, commands over 400 characters)
treatment: arm A class, arm B reviewer steps, arm C key steps and treated_core
generation_config: reuse_existing_server, number of stagings, port-normalised digests of the generation and the scoring-base config
references_renamed_selector: static scan of the delivered specs (True, False or None when it cannot be told)
cost: tokens: parent uncached/cached input and output, child uncached/cached input and output, processed (uncached input + output), total, completeness and sources
pipeline: tokens and elapsed seconds, arm B = source arm A plus reviewer call
cost_usd (Claude records: sum of modelUsage costUSD)

schedule: Entry preflights for all roster models first (roster order, one call at a time). Then one model at a time in roster order, admitted models only; within a model one call at a time with the same seeded two-phase algorithm as v1, recomputed for 4 repetitions: the 48 arm A and arm C cells first, then the 24 arm B cells, so that B always runs after the A cell it reviews. A v2 driver refuses to start while a v1 or v2 driver process exists, and holds a campaign lock file for its whole run.
combination_with_v1: The four Claude models of v1 and the Codex models of v2 are combined only descriptively, as juxtaposed per-model label tables and per-family counts (summary --v1-dir). No pooled p-value, no pooled N and no joint cross-model verdict is computed or implied across the two families unless the owner approves a written addendum before the v2 results are read. The v1 Codex rows are labelled harness-limited wherever shown. The pooled analysis (pooled_analysis) pools Codex v2 models only and never combines families.
stop_rules: One model call at a time across the whole campaign; load wait as in v1.
Stop when free disk is below 4 GiB, on a usage/rate limit, on any digest drift, or after three consecutive aborted cells.

Never edit this protocol, the README up to its '## Results' heading, the runner, the compat adapter, the v1 files or freeze.json after the first preflight or scheduled call (freeze.json may be deleted and recreated only before the first preflight call; the entry decisions are bound to it); a change needs a successor protocol.
drive proceeds only after the entry go/no-go: at least 4 admitted models over both lineages, unless the owner passes --descriptive-only.

drive refuses to start without a harness live check that passed and is bound to this freeze, and refuses to score while the generation staging wrapper is active or a case config differs from the frozen shape.
limits: 6 tasks x 4 repetitions per arm per model: tiny. The 6 tasks are the v1 synthetic fixtures with author-written faults.

The classifier is conservative by construction: official-tool needs positive evidence, and some genuine official runs classify as unverified. The primary view can therefore drop genuine cells; the upper view is the other bound.

The pinned official generator definition restricts playwright-test to 19 generator/browser tools and sets sandbox_mode read-only. Compat arm A carries that allowlist session-wide and requests the read-only sandbox for both the parent and its generic generating child because the v2 spawn interface cannot select the custom role. The child follows the generator definition and writes through generator_write_test; planner/healer MCP tools are excluded. Configuration acceptance, generic-child inheritance and direct-write denial are unverified offline. generator_write_test writes code verbatim, so authorship is not recovered from headers; official-tool still means observed generator MCP use, never proof of authorship.
The compat adapter changes arm B's flags too (no --ephemeral); the effect on B is not separated.

Child-agent tool calls are not in the parent's JSON event stream under multi_agent v2. The adapter now persists each cell's CODEX_HOME sessions and the classifier reads the child rollouts as its primary signal, but the rollout schema was read from host Codex CLI 0.157 to 0.159 rollouts, not from the container's build, and the persistence mount has never run live: until the harness live check passes, fidelity is inferred, not observed. Whether child token usage is additive to the parent's reported usage is a hint from the live check, not a verified fact.
The cross-model rule has low power by design of the per-model sign rule (see justification); 'not consistent' is not evidence of no effect.
Models run on different days and host loads; the model ids are provenance, not attestation. The host-local model catalog was read from the host cache, not from the container's own bundled catalog.
The authors read the stored cells of gpt-5.5 (pilots), gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-astra, claude-sonnet-5-5 and the compat-diag runs before writing this protocol; they did not read any other v1 model.

The primary view is a per-protocol analysis: arm A and B cells are selected on evidence that the tools ran (a post-randomization variable possibly correlated with outcome) while arm C is not. The power simulation ignores this selection. Fidelity in the stored v1 Codex cells was 0 to 3 of 12, so the primary view may be thin or empty for many models.

Possible effort confound: the host model catalog lists multi_agent_reasoning_effort 'xhigh' for gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-astra (none for the other roster models) while every cell is run at medium effort. Whether a spawned child inherits that setting, and so runs at a different effort than arm C's parent, was not verified; it is not recorded per cell.
The classifier regexes are tuned on a small stored sample and not validated on unseen transcripts; message evidence can still be a false positive (the entry rule needs hard evidence).

Generation-phase config: the model sees a webServer config with reuseExistingServer true while scoring uses false. This changes what the model observes when it runs its own tests (the port conflict is gone for every arm); it is not a treatment difference between arms, and it is not shown live to remove the conflict.

The as_treated view and the fidelity tables select on post-randomisation behaviour (per-protocol); step detection is textual and reads the parent stream only (a command run by a spawned agent is not seen); the scanner step counts an executed scan.sh, the mention count is kept beside it. They are sensitivities, not corrections of the primary view.

The headline metric is, empirically, a selector-hygiene indicator (see harness_fixes.H5). The secondary refactor classes that would separate hygiene from robustness are specified but not built (secondary_refactor_classes), so v2 results cannot yet say whether specs survive a text or structure change.

Token accounting assumes Codex counts cached tokens inside input_tokens and that cache_write_input_tokens (observed 0) is inside input_tokens too; child usage is additive to the parent's. The live check records the evidence; Claude is read from modelUsage, which includes subagents.

power_simulation.how: python3 scripts/evals/run-generator-multimodel-v2-codex.py power  (offline; deterministic: random.Random with a string seed)
power_simulation.model: Per replicate: task difficulty a_t ~ N(0,1) shared by all models; per model u ~ N(0,0.5); P(A cell survives) = expit(a_t + u); P(C cell survives) = expit(a_t + u + delta + shared task effect + lineage task effect), delta ~ N(effect, 0.5) for the fraction of models that carry the effect and 0 for the rest. Each A cell is official-tool with probability 'fidelity' (1.0, 0.75, 0.5 or 0.25), 4 repetitions per arm and task, per-model label by the v1 sign rule on refactor survival only (the guards are ignored, which upper-bounds each individual-model directional label probability within this simulated model; cross-model probabilities are simulation estimates, not upper bounds, because a guard can remove an opposing label and thereby create cross-model agreement), evaluable only with >= 6 official A cells on >= 5 tasks; then the cross-model rules are applied. Compositions: N models entered = 3 (2 gpt-6 + 1 gpt-5.6), 4 (2+2), 5 (3+2), 6 (4+2), 8 (4+4). Scenarios: null; null with a task effect shared by all models (sd 1.0); null with a task effect shared within a lineage (sd 1.5); effect 1.0 in all models; effect 2.4 (pilot size) in all; effect 2.4 in two thirds. Cells list [P(consistent X better), P(consistent opposite)] per rule and lineage requirement.
power_simulation.not_modelled: Correlation of arms across models caused by one shared harness artifact on the 6 fixtures (a real, systematic harness difference between arms looks like an effect to any cross-model rule on these tasks), B-arm dependence on A, the guards, and heterogeneity of cell success within a model beyond task and model offsets.

H1_port_conflict.what: In the generation phase every arm's staged project carries playwright.config.mjs with `reuseExistingServer: true` instead of the case's frozen `reuseExistingServer: false`. Nothing else in the config differs.
H1_port_conflict.why: In the v1 Claude campaign the parent's single verification run of `playwright test` failed with 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health is already used' in 12 of 12 sonnet arm-A cells before any test started: the official generator's MCP session keeps the app server alive on that port. Arms B and C did not hit it. On Codex, gpt-6-sol arm A reports the same symptom.
H1_port_conflict.scope: Generation only, all three arms identically (arm B's reviewer call is a generation-phase call). The swap is an engine.stage wrapper active only inside one_call; scoring stages through the unmodified engine.stage with the frozen configs (reuseExistingServer false, clean environment, so that a leftover server cannot serve the original app instead of a mutant). The deliverable is tests/ only, so the generation config cannot reach scoring through files.
H1_port_conflict.proof: Offline tests stage a project per arm through the real v1 one_call and assert: generation config true for A, B and C and identical across them (port-normalised digest), the same file staged by the scoring path is false, engine.stage is restored after every call (also on an exception), and `scoring_guard` refuses to score while the wrapper is active or if a case config is not the frozen shape. Each cell records the digests; analyze raises if one case has two generation digests.
H1_port_conflict.not_done: Not observed live: that reuseExistingServer true removes the port conflict for the Codex arm A. The live check does not exercise it. It is the first thing to read in the first preflight cells (a parent `playwright test` result without the 'is already used' error).

H2_command_truncation.problem: The v3 engine's compliance_from_events keeps str(command)[:400], so a long scanner invocation is missed (sonnet arm C scan.sh: engine 2 of 12, transcripts 6 of 12).
H2_command_truncation.change: The engine is bound by earlier freezes and is not edited. generator_v2_codex_evidence.compliance_from_events reads the raw transcript (Codex command_execution items and Claude stream-json tool_use blocks) and never cuts a command. scanner_runs keeps the engine's definition (the command mentions scan.sh) for comparability; scanner_exec_runs counts invocations where scan.sh is the script of a bash/sh call. Each cell also records the longest command and how many exceed 400 characters.
H2_command_truncation.verified_offline: Synthetic long command; and a read-only run over the 12 stored sonnet arm C transcripts of the audit (6 of 12 mention the scanner).
H2_command_truncation.claude_note: The same function reads the Claude dialect, so a Claude successor can reuse it.

H3_child_agents.problem: Codex child agents (spawn_agent) are not visible in the parent `codex exec --json` stream: their MCP calls and token usage are missing from every Codex record. The '// spec:' and '// seed:' headers are not evidence of MCP use.
H3_child_agents.change: The adapter persists each call's CODEX_HOME sessions (rollouts of the parent and every child) per cell. generator_v2_codex_evidence parses them: completed MCP calls per server and tool (event_msg item_completed McpToolCall; also the older mcp_tool_call_end event and mcp__server__tool function calls as a fallback; fallback completion requires a matching structured success result, explicit errors fail and ambiguous outputs remain unverified), parent/child links from session_meta, cumulative token usage per thread. The arm A classifier uses a completed generator_* or browser_* call on the playwright-test server in the parent stream or any rollout as the PRIMARY signal (test_* and planner_* calls are information only). With a complete rollout record (root identified, unique spawn IDs and parent relationships reconciled across every descendant, no unresolved spawn identities or duplicate thread rollouts, clean census), absence of a call is an observation and the secondary evidence (.playwright-mcp/ files, affirming messages) cannot turn the cell positive (a disagreement is recorded as signal_conflict). Without a complete record (rollouts not persisted, as in stored v1 cells, or observation gaps) the secondary evidence applies.
H3_child_agents.schema_basis: Rollout structure read from Codex CLI 0.157 to 0.159 rollouts on the host (types and keys only). The container's Codex build may differ; this is what the live check settles.

live_check.name: harness live check (command: harness-check --allow-live [--model <id>]; preflight runs it first and refuses to run any entry call until it passes; drive refuses without a pass bound to the freeze)
live_check.call: One arm-A-shaped call (playwright-test MCP server declared session-wide, sessions persisted) on the unscheduled task v2-01 with a dedicated prompt: spawn exactly one native agent whose only job is one `test_list` call of the playwright-test server (no browser, no file written, per playwright 1.62.0 lib/mcp/test/testTools.js), wait, finish with status `other`. Timeout 420 s, one call.
pass_requires_all_of: call_ok (no infrastructure error or timeout, transcript present)
root_rollout_identified (the parent's rollout, by the thread id of the stream)
persistence_census_clean (no skipped or errored file in the cell's persistence census)
child_rollout_found (a rollout whose parent chain leads to the root)
spawns_have_rollouts (unique spawn IDs in the parent and all descendants match persisted parent relationships; unknown identities and duplicate thread rollouts fail)
child_called_test_list (a completed playwright-test.test_list call in a child rollout)
child_token_usage_present (child usage total above 0 in every child rollout)
live_check.inconclusive: Sessions persisted and the root found, but the model spawned no child, or the child made no test_list call: model behaviour, rerun with another model (--model). Not a statement about persistence.
live_check.aborted: An infrastructure outcome (rate limit, output-schema error, container error): says nothing about persistence; rerun when healthy.
live_check.fail: The call timed out, the sessions were not persisted, the root or child usage could not be parsed, the census has skipped or errored files, or the parent stream shows a completed spawn without a persisted child rollout: the harness is broken; do not rely on this freeze (delete freeze.json, fix, refreeze, rerun the check).
live_check.order: freeze first (every campaign live command needs freeze.json; the separate non-data smoke command does not and the result is bound to its digest), then harness-check, then preflight. If code must change after a failed check, delete freeze.json and refreeze; an earlier freeze's result is never reused.
recorded_informational: parent_stream_blind_to_child (no mcp_tool_call in the parent stream: confirms the premise)

parent_usage_matches_root_rollout (parent stream usage equals the parent's own rollout total: hints that child tokens are NOT folded into the parent usage, so the pipeline sums parent plus children; a mismatch must be read before cost totals are quoted)
live_check.cost: One short call of one model; the result is kept in _entry/harness-check.json bound to the freeze and is never data.
live_check.role_check: The diagnostic uses its own test_list-only MCP allowlist under read-only sandbox, not the generator allowlist. Before campaign reliance, verify the ordinary arm-A allowlist is accepted, child sandbox inherits read-only, planner/healer tools are invisible, shell writes are denied and generator_write_test can deliver specs.

H3_child_agents.approval: approved 2026-10-15: per-cell CODEX_HOME sessions persistence is the primary arm-A fidelity signal and the source of child token usage; message/artifact evidence remains secondary.

H4_treatment_fidelity_arm_c.problem: Claude arm C was a minimal treatment on sonnet: SKILL.md read 12/12 but no reference file (0/12), no preflight (0/12), no browser exploration (0/12), scan.sh 6/12, an independent review 1/12, self-reported complete 0/12, about 55 s per cell. The v1 adapter stages the skill in a temp directory and passes --disable-slash-commands, so the model must read files by hand.
H4_treatment_fidelity_arm_c.change_in_this_protocol: Codex arm C is unchanged (the Codex CLI has no equivalent flag; the staged skill and the prompt line are v1's). Its key steps are now measured from the raw transcript for every cell and reported (fidelity table, evidence.C_STEPS), and the as_treated view restricts arm C to cells that ran the core steps.
H4_treatment_fidelity_arm_c.successor_requirement_claude: A Claude successor must install the skill as a real project skill (for example .claude/skills/<name>/ inside the cell project), keep the Skill tool available for the arms that are meant to have a skill, and verify from the init event of every call that exactly the intended skills are listed (none for the official-generator arm). Not built here: it needs the Claude adapter and a live call.

H5_headline_metric.problem: 'Refactor survival' is essentially 'the spec references no pre-refactor #id or .class selector': in the audited campaign 23 of 23 clean cells that referenced one failed the refactor and 0 of 62 that did not.
H5_headline_metric.change: The primary metric is unchanged. summary prints it as what it is: a per-arm 2x2 on the clean cells (references a renamed #id/.class: yes/no, by refactor outcome), computed by a static scan of the delivered specs' string literals against the ids and classes the case's refactor renames, plus the clean-conditional survival (survival among clean cells).

harness_fixes.H6_cost_accounting: cost_endpoints in results.json and the summary: parent tokens from the stream (else the root rollout), child tokens from rollouts, uncached input, cached input and output separately; arm B pipeline = its source arm A cell plus the reviewer call; Claude tokens and cost from modelUsage (inputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens uncached, cacheReadInputTokens cached, costUSD). See cost_endpoints.
harness_fixes.H7_fidelity_tables: The fidelity table (arm A MCP evidence and rollout counts, arm B reviewer steps, arm C key steps) is printed with every model's labels, and the as_treated view is computed next to the primary view. Definitions are in fidelity.treatment, fixed in advance.

pooled_analysis.written: before any successor data is scored; bound in the freeze through this file
pooled_analysis.motivation: The frozen v1 per-model sign rule (same sign in at least 5 of 6 tasks) has about 23% power per model for a pilot-sized effect and the cross-model rule at most about 4% in the v1 line (v2's own simulation is in power_simulation). A pooled analysis that uses the size of the effect, with models and tasks as clusters, is the pre-registered complement. It does not replace the rule and issues no verdict.
pooled_analysis.metrics_note: refactor_score (the headline metric) is the primary metric and is reported in every listed view; the other two are reported in the primary view only.
pooled_analysis.pool: Complete models whose contrast is evaluable in the view (the cross-model rule's own eligibility); incomplete models are excluded, as in the rule.
pooled_analysis.unit: Model-by-task: per task the mean metric of arm X cells minus that of arm Y cells in the view, for tasks where both arms have a cell; repetitions are averaged inside a task.
pooled_analysis.estimate: Unweighted mean over models of each model's unweighted mean over its tasks (every model counts once, regardless of how many cells its view keeps).
pooled_analysis.sign_flip: Exact two-sided sign-flip enumeration over models: all 2^N sign patterns of the N model effects, p = share of patterns whose absolute mean reaches the observed one. Null calibration requires the joint distribution of effects to be invariant under every coordinate-wise sign flip, making all sign patterns equally likely conditional on magnitudes; marginal symmetry alone is insufficient. Shared task or lineage shocks can correlate signs and violate this assumption, so these p-values are not calibrated under such correlated effects and remain development evidence. The smallest attainable p is 2/2^N: 0.03125 at N = 6 and never below 0.125 at N <= 4, which is printed beside every p.

cluster_bootstrap.resampling: crossed: models drawn with replacement and tasks drawn with replacement, the estimate recomputed on the resampled grid, percentile interval; a draw with no value is skipped and counted. With 4 to 6 models and 6 tasks this interval under-covers and is shown as a spread, not a guarantee.

pooled_analysis.robustness: per-model effects, models positive and negative, lineage means, per-task profile across models, leave-one-model-out estimates.

owner_approval.note: approved 2026-10-15: model and task clusters, unweighted model mean, exact model sign-flip, two-way cluster bootstrap, ITT and as-treated views are pre-registered analysis. All pooled results are development evidence, never replacing per-model labels. The protocol and approval are bound at freeze.
owner_approval.pooling_with_v1_claude_family_note: Declarative: no code reads this flag and the code never pools across families.

pooled_analysis.reporting: summary (Pooled analysis section) and <root>/pooled.json, every pooled result labelled development evidence; no pooled verdict or replacement of per-model labels.
pooled_analysis.successor_alignment: A Claude successor protocol must carry this section unchanged (same unit, estimate, tests, seed and owner flags) so that the families can be compared descriptively without a joint verdict.

cost_endpoints.co_primary: Cost is read next to quality, never alone: (1) refactor survivors per 100k processed tokens ('quality per 100k tokens'), (2) pipeline seconds (mean per cell and per survivor), both reported in every view.
cost_endpoints.processed_tokens: uncached input + output, parent and child agents together. Cached input is excluded from the co-primary denominator and reported separately; the same ratio with cached input added is printed as a sensitivity (quality_per_100k_total).
cost_endpoints.pipeline: Arm A and arm C: the call itself. Arm B: its source arm A cell plus the reviewer call (the reviewer pass costs the generation it reviews). Arm B cells whose source is missing are incomplete. Every call attempt is included once, including infrastructure retries; missing per-attempt token records make the cell incomplete.
cost_endpoints.ratio_of_sums: survivors in the cells with complete token records divided by the sum of their tokens (not a mean of per-cell ratios); cells with incomplete tokens are counted but excluded.

token_sources.codex: parent: its own persisted root rollout when available, else stream turn.completed usage retained as a cross-check; children: persisted child rollouts cumulative usage (approved 2026-10-15). uncached input = input_tokens - cached_input_tokens. Incomplete rollout/token records are excluded from cost ratios and counted. Malformed rollouts, unlinked children, extra roots, missing root usage, skipped/error persistence and missing observed spawns, unresolved spawn identities, duplicate thread rollouts and mismatched parent relationships make token records incomplete.
token_sources.claude: modelUsage: inputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens uncached, cacheReadInputTokens cached, outputTokens, costUSD; subagents are inside modelUsage.

cost_endpoints.pooled_use: none; the pooled analysis is on quality metrics only.

secondary_refactor_classes.why_not_built_here: Building and validating them needs a browser and local app servers (ARIA snapshots before and after each edit list, and a reference spec run), which the offline-only task that wrote this section did not allow; shipping unvalidated edit lists into a freeze would be worse than shipping none.

R-TEXT.intent: A visible-text or label change that leaves DOM structure, ids, classes and roles alone: button labels, headings, field labels, status messages.
R-TEXT.edits: one edit list per case in the form of truth/<case>.json `refactor` (find/replace on app.mjs, every marker unique), authored from app.mjs only.
R-TEXT.acceptance: (1) the edit list applies (each marker occurs exactly once); (2) the ARIA snapshot of every route has identical roles, hierarchy and order and differs only in the names/text of the listed nodes; (3) ids and classes unchanged (the manifest `renamed_ids_and_classes` is empty); (4) at least 3 distinct labels per case change.
R-TEXT.metric: refactor_text_score = 1 if the spec passes its clean runs and the refactored app, else 0 (same shape as refactor_score).

R-STRUCT.intent: A DOM-structure change that keeps roles and accessible names: wrapper elements added or removed, containers changed (div to section, list to grid), siblings regrouped, without changing any id or class.
R-STRUCT.edits: as above, authored from app.mjs only, before any arm's spec is read.
R-STRUCT.acceptance: (1) the edit list applies; (2) the ARIA snapshot of every route is byte-identical before and after (roles, names, order); (3) ids and classes unchanged; (4) at least one change per case alters a parent-child or sibling relation that a descendant-combinator, nth-child or XPath selector would depend on.

secondary_refactor_classes.build_procedure: Author the edit lists blind (no arm output opened); run the acceptance checks with the engine's aria_snapshots on the original and the edited app; additionally run each case's existing seed spec against both versions (it must pass on both); record the lists' digests in a successor freeze. Score as secondary metrics through engine.evaluate_specs-style runs with the same load, retry and port rules as the primary refactor.
secondary_refactor_classes.use: Secondary metrics only: reported per arm and view beside the headline metric and eligible for the pooled analysis as additional metrics; they never enter a per-model label or the cross-model rule, and they never replace the primary metric.

call_budget.time_note: Serial nominal call-timeout budget: 30 h per model, 180 h scored calls across six models, 185 h 7 min including up to 12 real entry calls and one harness check. This is not an elapsed-time prediction or hard bound: setup, scoring, load waits, infrastructure retries and repeated harness checks are additional. Fewer admitted models reduce scored calls. Separate smoke calls are not included.

smoke.output: Required --output directory outside the repository, outside ~/.cache/e2e-skills-bench and outside resolved configured Codex successor and inherited campaign roots (including environment overrides); reject symlink components and resolve paths and refuse forbidden paths before any call or write. No campaign cache/status/entry artifacts.
smoke.models: Repeatable --model, six-model roster only, default first roster model; gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-luna cannot be selected.
smoke.analysis: Never scored, never imported by analyze or summary; non-data schema and markers refuse benchmark ingestion. Does not satisfy freeze-bound harness-check or entry decisions.
smoke.execution_status: not run in the offline build; no freeze created.
